newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down on Wednesday but early-maturing contracts bucked the trend in active trading due to a new domestic A share issue on Friday, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract rose to 13.20 percent from 12.51 percent on Tuesday.
Turnover shrank to 5.99 million lots from 8.47 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said institutions borrowed short-term money on the market to prepare for the A share issue of Shanghai Worldbest Industry Development Co on Friday.
"The early-maturing contracts are likely to continue to be firm with a new A share issue today and another on Friday, which are sucking out short-term funds," said one trader.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down in slow trading on weak market sentiment after prices having fallen for more than two weeks, traders said.
The newest three-year bond that listed in late August and will mature in August 1999 was the most active contract today, losing 0.24 yuan to close at a record low of 103.83 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market was very low at 913,090 lots from 1.16 million on Tuesday.
